hook: SCP-3005 is presented as whatever survived a data loss: a few corrupted fragments of procedure and one test log that is supposedly complete. Read the log the way you would read any routine list of Foundation experiments, and keep an eye on the format itself. The less you know beforehand, the better it works.
whyItMatters: The file belongs to a strand of the wiki that makes the document itself the medium of horror: the anomaly is never described, and you only see what it does to the record and to the person writing it. Its tags, including esoteric-class, meta, psychological-horror and fifthist, point straight at that ambition. The Uncontained (Unknown) class sets the mood before the log even begins.
thingsToNotice:
The blank template at the top of the log is the trick. Once you have seen what each field should hold, you notice every time a field starts holding the wrong thing: numbers get doubled, quantities are spelled out in odd ways, and the number five shows up more and more. The researcher's comments drift from tidy observations to confusion about who is who, and the outputs stop being objects and start being ideas.

After finishing, go back to the corrupted procedures at the very top. The instruction about handling casualties takes on a new meaning once you have seen how the log repeats a related phrase, and the last entries show the document itself giving way.

related.note: Another file where the text itself is where the hazard shows.
A recovered first-person record that unravels as you read it.
